known_facts_book1: A small, dried-up woman of the Yip Country whose diamond-studded gold dishpan is stolen on the very morning Ozma disappears.
The dishpan belonged to her mother and all her grandmothers since the beginning of time, and is the oldest thing in the Yip Country.
It has magic powers: whoever owns it is a good cook, and without it her cookies burn, come out too tough to eat, or are no better than any other woman's.
Raises such a hue and cry over the theft that the Yips force her to take the matter to the Frogman.
Sets out alone rather than give up, and nine young Yips come partway down the mountain with her before the great gulf turns them back.
Is carried over the gulf on the Frogman's back, clinging where his neck ought to be, since he has no neck at all.
Refuses flatly to bathe in the Truth Pond, saying that if she told the truth the Frogman would not like her.
Sees an image of her dishpan conjured by the Bear King and throws her arms around it, finding nothing there at all.
Never recovers the dishpan herself: Ugu flees with it, and the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman find it lying under a tree in the Quadling Country and bring it to Ozma, who gives it back to her.
Stays on at the Emerald City afterward, in no hurry to return to the Yip Country.

known_relations_book1.the Frogman: Her companion and adviser, whose boasted wisdom she believed in.
known_relations_book1.Ugu the Shoemaker: The magician who stole her dishpan and used it to steal everything else.
known_relations_book1.the Lavender Bear: The King whose magic shows her both her dishpan and the thief.
known_relations_book1.Ozma: Who promises the dishpan's return and keeps the promise.

known_facts_book1: Descended from the common frogs of Oz; he was carried off by a bird as a small frog, wriggled free, and fell into a hidden enchanted pool on the Yip tableland.
Grew huge and unusually intelligent by feeding on the magic **skosh** found nowhere else on earth except that one pool.
Stands upright on his hind legs, dresses in yellow satin plush breeches, a bright yellow swallow-tailed coat, green stockings and red shoes with diamond buckles, and carries a gold-headed cane.
Wears great gold-rimmed spectacles not because his eyes are bad but because they make him look wise.
Is the Yips' adviser and leader; when he does not know a thing he pretends to, which the Yips find answers just as well, and he knows in his heart he is a humbug.
Joins Cayke's quest out of ambition to be admired beyond the Yip Country, not out of kindness.
Bathes by accident in the **Truth Pond**, whose golden plate reads that whoever bathes in the water must always afterward tell the truth — and can no longer claim to be wise.
Confesses to Cayke that he is not the Wisest Creature in the World and is not wise at all, which shatters one of her most pleasing illusions.
Is fed a dose of zosozo by the Wizard and leaps the Wall of Steel in three bounds, sticking in the pin that destroys it.
Fights the giant Dove of War bare-handed to protect Dorothy, bearing it to the floor at the first leap, and has his fine clothes torn by its talons.
Becomes a favorite at the Emerald City at the end.

known_relations_book1.Cayke: The Cookie Cook he accompanies and whose illusions about him he destroys.
known_relations_book1.the Truth Pond: The enchanted water that ends his career as a humbug.
known_relations_book1.the Wizard: Who gives him zosozo and sends him over the Wall of Steel.
known_relations_book1.Dorothy: Whom he protects from the Dove of War, not knowing the Magic Belt already shields her.
known_relations_book1.Scraps: The first of the Emerald City party he meets, on the hilltop.

not_in_this_book: the Frogman refuses to admit he is not wise
